result.title: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning
result.summary: Selecting high-quality training data can reduce computation cost for LLM fine-tuning. Prior work on data selection developed a variety of difficulty-based scores, motivated by the intuition that harder examples are more informative. While effective for smaller classification models, we find that such methods often fail to outperform random selection for LLM fine-tuning. Our analysis reveals that random selection performs better because it is more representative of the underlying input space---i.e., has better coverage. To validate the importance of coverage, we implement a simple clustering-based selection method which selects data that is more representative of the underlying input distribution. On a set of diverse single-domain tasks, this method yields performance at or above that of random selection. On the diverse, multi-domain Tülu 3 mixture, where random sampling no longer guarantees a balanced subset, our method outperforms all methods. Overall, our results indicate that prioritizing coverage over difficulty leads to more effective data selection for LLM fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 该文发现难度导向的数据选择在 LLM 微调中常不如随机采样，据此提出基于聚类的、强调覆盖输入分布的选样方法，并在单领域任务与 Tülu 3 多领域混合数据上验证其效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“覆盖优于难度”的选样准则可供核查 LVR 训练数据（如推理轨迹、视觉证据样本）的筛选与多源混合配比，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
